title: Exact coefficient-model realizations intertwine the derived comparisons
statement: For a scheme X [def-pc-scheme] and a commutative ring A in the coefficient universe, constant-scalar restriction from modules over the sheafified constant ring to fixed-A module sheaves [def-pe-etale-constructible-module] is an equivalence. Compose it with evaluation on the original sites through AsSmall to define E and G on the etale and pro-etale coefficient models [lem-pe-coefficient-comparison-data]. These are additive equivalences. They intertwine the specified model comparison inverse image with the ordinary comparison inverse image [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For every functor D equipped with the localization factorization Q_et followed by D isomorphic to the specified complex pullback followed by Q_pro, there is a natural isomorphism D(E) followed by the ordinary derived comparison to D followed by D(G). Both standard model derived categories are in the specified coefficient-derived universe.

source.place: opening paragraph: coefficient identification before invoking finite-Tor comparison

proof.text: Forgetting commutativity commutes with constant-ring sheafification. Restriction along that ring isomorphism followed by constant-ring restriction has the same scalar action as coefficientModelFixedScalars, because the two sheafification units agree. Its identity additive maps give the natural comparison. Apply the constant-ring module equivalence.

Compose constant-scalar restriction with the inverse AsSmall sheaf equivalences to construct E and G. The latter preserve the original sections and maps. Equivalences preserve finite limits, finite colimits, and addition.

The ring comparison extends the constant-section unit, by the sheafification adjunction equation. Thus model direct image followed by E equals G followed by ordinary direct image on sections and scalar actions. Compose adjunctions with E and G, conjugate the right-adjoint square, and use uniqueness of left adjoints to obtain the inverse-image square.

Exactness of the model pullback permits termwise derived localization of the square. The supplied factorization of D identifies it with the derived exact functor using the fully faithful localization universal property. Whisker that identification with D(G).

theorem finiteComparisonModelDerivedSquare :
    letI : HasDerivedCategory.{u + 2} (ConstantCompletion.Mod (ConstantCompletion.constant
        (Scheme.smallModelComparisonEtaleTopology.{u, u + 1} X) A)) :=
      HasDerivedCategory.standard _
    letI : HasDerivedCategory.{u + 2} (ConstantCompletion.Mod (ConstantCompletion.constant
        (Scheme.coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, u + 1} X) A)) :=
      HasDerivedCategory.standard _
    ∀ D : ConstantCompletion.D (ConstantCompletion.constant
        (Scheme.smallModelComparisonEtaleTopology.{u, u + 1} X) A) ⥤
          ConstantCompletion.D (ConstantCompletion.constant
            (Scheme.coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, u + 1} X) A),
      Nonempty (ConstantCompletion.Q _ ⋙ D ≅
        constructibleComparisonComplexPullback.{u, u + 1} X A ⋙ ConstantCompletion.Q _) →
      Nonempty ((finiteComparisonEtaleModelRealization X A).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
          (comparisonUpperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) X).mapDerivedCategory ≅
        D ⋙ (finiteComparisonProEtaleModelRealization X A).mapDerivedCategory)
